steps.message:
# Audit the production releases against change tickets

Change requests and incidents are tickets in the `tickets` service. Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service. The change audit policy is published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

It is now 2026-09-24T09:00:00Z. Run the change audit for the period from 2026-09-21T00:00:00Z (included) to 2026-09-24T00:00:00Z (not included), as the change audit policy in force says: check every audited `prod` release against the change tickets, roll back what the policy allows, and record the result on the tickets. The docs service also keeps superseded documents; follow the one in force.

- Only `prod` is in scope. Do not deploy anything, do not touch `staging`, and do not change tickets the policy does not tell you to change.
- Every `rollback` call creates a new release and moves one release further back, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

Write `/app/change-audit.json` as:

```json
{"uncovered": ["<release id>", ...], "rolled_back": {"<service>": "<commit now live in prod>", ...}, "needs_review": ["<service>", ...]}
```

`uncovered` lists every audited release that no ticket covers, in any order. `rolled_back` has an entry for every service you rolled back at least once. `needs_review` lists, in alphabetical order, the services that needed remediation and whose live `prod` commit is still not cleared when you stop.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"id":"change-audit-policy","title":"Change audit policy","tags":["audit","ops","release"],"updated_at":"2026-09-01","body":"# Change audit policy

Revision 3. Status: current, in force since 2026-09-01. Replaces revision 2.

Every production release must be covered by an approved change ticket. The weekly change audit checks the `prod` releases of an audit period against the change tickets, rolls back what this policy allows, and records the result on the tickets. Times are UTC.

## Change tickets

A change ticket is labeled `change`. Its body describes the change:

    Service: <service>
    Commit: <commit>
    Type: standard | emergency
    Window: <start> to <end>      (standard changes only)
    Supersedes: #<ticket id>      (only when the ticket replaces an earlier one)
    Requested by: <handle>

A change ticket names a release when its `Service` and `Commit` lines match the release's service and commit. A ticket's status does not affect coverage.

An approval is a ticket comment whose body starts with the word `Approved`, written by a CAB member. CAB members: `m.campos`, `r.leiva`, `s.ortiz`. Comments by anyone else approve nothing.

## Audited releases

The audited releases are the `prod` releases created in the audit period, except releases created by a rollback. In `status` history a release created by a rollback directly follows (is newer than) a release whose status is `rolled_back`. `staging` releases are not audited.

## Coverage

A ticket covers a release it names when:

- standard change: the release was created inside the ticket's window, start and end included, and a CAB member approved the ticket before the release was created;
- emergency change: a CAB member approved the ticket before the release was created or at most 24 hours after it. Emergency changes ship first and are approved after the fact.

Superseded tickets: a ticket named in the `Supersedes` line of another change ticket is superseded. It covers nothing, whatever its approvals and its status; only the superseding ticket counts.

Earlier approval: a release of a commit that a covered release of the same service already ran in `prod` earlier in the audit period is covered by the same ticket as that release, wherever its window ends.

An audited release that no ticket covers is uncovered.

## Remediation

A commit is cleared for a service when a covered release of that service in the audit period ran it, or when it was the live `prod` release of the service when the audit period started.

A service needs remediation when its live `prod` release is an uncovered audited release. For each such service, roll `prod` back one `rollback` call at a time, reading the live release after each call, until the live commit is cleared. A rollback returns to the release that the live one replaced (`previous_release_id` in `status`), and each call moves one release further back. Stop earlier, and leave the service where it is, when:

- the live release runs a build that an `open` incident ticket for that service pins (its `Pinned build` line). Rolling back would take `prod` below the pinned build. Incident tickets in any other status pin nothing.
- the live release has no previous release to return to.

Never roll back any other service, even when an earlier release of the period was uncovered.

## Recording the audit

Every change ticket that names at least one audited release, except a superseded ticket, gets exactly one comment:

- `audit: covered <release ids>` when the ticket covers every audited release it names;
- `audit: not covered <release ids>` otherwise; then also set the ticket's status to `pending`.

`<release ids>` lists every audited release the ticket names, separated by commas. Leave every other ticket unchanged: superseded tickets, incident tickets, and change tickets that name no audited release.
"}

{"id":"change-audit-policy-r2","title":"Change audit policy (revision 2)","tags":["audit","ops","release"],"updated_at":"2026-04-06","body":"# Change audit policy (revision 2)

Revision 2. Status: superseded by revision 3 on 2026-09-01. Kept for reference only.

Every production release needs an approved change ticket. Standard changes deploy inside their window after approval. Emergency changes are approved within 72 hours after the release.

Uncovered releases still live in `prod` are rolled back until the live release is covered.

Record `audit ok` or `audit failed` on each change ticket.
"}

steps.reasoning_content:
I'm checking each of the two items against its approval and covering ticket: the auth change at 16:00 on 09-21 is inside the window and approved, so it's covered, and the billing changes fall under ticket 902 and the earlier-approval rule.

Going through the cart release next: r-160 went out at 11:00 on 09-22, but its approval only came at 11:40, so it isn't covered, and the fix is to roll back to r-132, which was already live at period start and is clean. Then the catalog change at r-163 is covered by the 905 window, since it was approved that morning, and the checkout emergency change at r-156 falls within the 24-hour approval window.

I'm moving through the search checks now: r-158 was approved by t.bravo rather than the CAB, so it's uncovered, and r-171 has no ticket at all. Since the live release runs build b-90 rather than the pinned b-83, I'd roll back once to r-158, which puts the pinned build live and stops the rollback, and flag search-api for review.

I'm going through the remaining services in this list: the edge ticket names a commit with no matching release, so there's nothing to audit there, and auth is already covered. The session release at 09-24 is outside the period, so I'm leaving it out. Across everything, seven releases are uncovered, and search-api is the only service that still needs review since its live commit hasn't been cleared.

Next I'm going through the orders and pricing releases, and the search rollback has to wait until I've sorted out which items still need a pending decision.

steps.message:
The audit is finished. I followed revision 3 of the policy, which is the one in force. Revision 2 is superseded.

**Uncovered releases (7):** r-160, r-173, r-165, r-169, r-147, r-158, r-171.

**Rollbacks (prod only):**

| Service | Rollbacks | Live commit now |
|---|---|---|
| cart-svc | 1 | `4de5424d` |
| ledger-api | 1 | `cfd636b6` |
| pricing-svc | 1 | `9da62630` |
| orders-api | 2 (r-169 → r-165 → r-151) | `1d172542` |
| search-api | 1 | `b864ea18` |

**search-api needs review.** I stopped it at r-179, which runs build b-83. The open incident INC-3312 (#922) pins b-83. The live commit `b864ea18` is not cleared, because its only ticket (#912) was approved by t.bravo, who is not a CAB member.

**Ticket records:**
- **Covered:** #901, #902, #905, #906 and #908 each got an `audit: covered …` comment.
- **Not covered:** #903, #907, #911 and #912 each got an `audit: not covered …` comment and were set to `pending`.
- **Left unchanged:** the superseded tickets #904 and #909, and #910 and #913, which name no audited release.

The results are in `/app/change-audit.json` and `/app/STATUS.json`. I set the status to `success`, since every step of the audit was completed.
